subject: general
question: What happens if you start a new blank presentation while another presentation is already open in MS PowerPoint?

options.text: A new MS PowerPoint window opens with the blank presentation.
MS PowerPoint displays an error message.
The slides from the current presentation are copied to the new one.

solution:
The Correct answer is __**A new MS PowerPoint window opens with the blank presentation.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When you start a new blank presentation in **MS PowerPoint** while another presentation is already open, it opens in a **new window.**
 
• This feature allows users to work on multiple presentations **simultaneously** without closing the current one.
 
• **MS PowerPoint** is designed to handle multiple windows, making it easier for users to copy content, compare slides, or work on different projects concurrently.
 
• Each presentation window operates independently, meaning changes in one presentation will not affect another unless content is explicitly copied and pasted.
 
• This functionality is useful in collaborative or multitasking environments where users may need to reference or edit multiple presentations.
 
• The ability to open multiple windows is a key feature of **Microsoft Office** applications, including PowerPoint, Word, and Excel.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **MS PowerPoint Error Messages**__

 __
 
• Option 2 mentions an error message, but **MS PowerPoint** does not display an error when opening a new blank presentation alongside an existing one.
 
• Error messages are typically displayed in situations such as file corruption, compatibility issues, or software bugs.
 
 
 
• **Closing Presentations Automatically**__
 __
 
• Option 3 suggests that the current presentation closes automatically, which is incorrect as **MS PowerPoint** retains the current presentation when a new one is opened.
 
• This behavior ensures users do not lose unsaved work.
 
 
 
• **Copying Slides Automatically**__
 
 
• Option 4 suggests that slides are copied automatically from the current presentation to the new one, which is not a default feature.
 
• Slides can be copied manually by the user using the **copy-paste functionality** in PowerPoint.
